text:
The largest recorded tree-cover loss event on this property was in **2020**, at about **67.7 ha**. The other events were 25.5 ha in 2015, 4.8 ha in 2017 and 0.8 ha in 2008 (Hansen Global Forest Change, 2001-2025 series).

- All four events fall before the 2020-12-31 baseline, so they are history rather than events in the monitoring period. After the baseline, only 0.4 ha of loss in 2021 was observed, in patches below the 0.5 ha minimum, so it isn't counted as an event.
- The events total about 98.8 ha, but tree cover in 2000 was only 23.0 ha. That mismatch is unexplained, so treat the event sizes with caution. It could reflect the canopy threshold or how the layers were measured.
- The JRC 2020 reference shows 0 ha of forest on the property.
